page: Microsoft Azure B16as_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz, providing 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Virtualization is handled via Microsoft Hyper-V, and the CPU supports vector instructions including AVX, FMA, and BMI2, alongside hardware acceleration for AES and SHA cryptography. The instance contains no bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core and memory subsystem capabilities. In synthetic CPU evaluations, stress-ng single-core performance ranks in the top 25 percent, while PassMark memory metrics also land in the upper quartile. Large multi-core compute tests, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and PassMark CPU tests, register squarely in the middle 50 percent bracket. In application-focused metrics, the instance achieves 14.29 GB/sec of static web serving throughput and handles 16.61 million Redis SET operations per second.

Because the B16as_v2 relies on a burstable CPU credit model, its cost profile offers high resource density for fluctuating compute requirements. It provides 64 GB of memory and 16 vCPUs without the cost baseline of fully dedicated compute nodes. However, workloads requiring sustained maximum CPU utilization may deplete burst capacity over time. This configuration is well matched for development environments, continuous integration agents, microservices hosting, intermediate relational databases, and burst-heavy web application tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure B16as_v2 is a general-purpose, burstable virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at up to 3.525 GHz. Configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 resource ratio under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Hardware features include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, though the server includes no local ephemeral storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing indicates strong single-core compute and high memory throughput, with multi-core metrics and database operations placing in the middle performance quartile. The burstable CPU architecture makes the B16as_v2 a cost-effective choice for intermittent workloads, continuous integration builders, development environments, and moderate web application serving that experience variable traffic patterns rather than constant peak CPU saturation.
